description: Frozen answers for outbound lane scheduling, derived from the ratified 70/20/10 share-and-donate model stated in `reconciled`, applied to lane-trace.json. The shared LaneScheduler implements the model and all three Rust arms (rust-packer, rust-driver, rust-ea) assert every case against this file; rust-packer reproduces it step for step, which keeps the model the scheduler's documented policy rather than a restatement of it. The swift-ea and kotlin-bt files are frozen captures of deleted code: they answer the 17 original cases as the corpus stood at capture time (lane_depth 64 on the two saturating cases) and answer neither wide-normal-frames-do-not-end-the-emission-for-waiting-bulk nor a-bulk-head-wider-than-its-share-is-not-starved-by-a-fed-normal-lane, both of which declare their arms in the corpus. An arm conforms when its lane-trace.<arm>.json matches these constants and the conformance-bearing fields of every step of every case it answers.

reconciled.lane_shares: 70/20/10, ratified, and the shares are ADDITIVE ALLOWANCES over one emission, not a partition of it. An emission takes a seed frame from the highest-priority non-empty lane, then walks the lanes in priority order with a running ceiling of `len(batch) + floor(max_emission_bytes * share)` clamped to max_emission_bytes, taking whole frames while they fit. Because each ceiling is relative to the batch length at the time that lane is visited, a lane that uses none of its share does not enlarge the next lane's share; the three allowances sum to the whole ceiling. Integer basis math (floor of max*pct/100) is the ruling; it is bit-identical to OutboundPacker's f32 `(max as f32 * share) as usize` on every ceiling this corpus produces (32768 -> 22937/6553/3276, 262144 -> 183500/52428/26214, 4096 -> 2867/819/409, 512 -> 358/102/51, 256 -> 179/51/25), so the daemon needs no change and the shared core does not inherit a float.
reconciled.seed_frame_is_free: The seed frame is placed before the share pass and is not charged against its own lane's allowance, so the highest-priority non-empty lane effectively gets seed + 70 percent. This is what makes strict-priority-baseline emit n0 first even though g0 arrived first, and it is the one-frame overshoot that keeps an oversize frame shippable at all. Ruled: keep it, and state it, because it is invisible in the packer source.
reconciled.donation_pass: After the share pass, a second pass walks the lanes in priority order with the ceiling at max_emission_bytes so idle lanes donate their unused allowance. Donation is what lets a single 16384-byte bulk frame ship at all when the bulk share is 6553 (byte-size-skewed-loads emission 1) and what fills the emission when only one lane is live (idle-lower-lanes-donate-to-normal, idle-normal-lane-donates-to-bulk, both 32768). Without it a bulk transfer would run at 20 percent of an otherwise silent link.
reconciled.emission_aborts_on_a_non_fitting_head: RATIFIED (Joey, 2026-08-05): a non-fitting head no longer ends the emission. `fill` leaves the frame at its lane's head and the pass advances to the next lane, in the share pass and the donation pass alike; the emission ends only when no lane has a head that fits in the remaining max_emission_bytes budget. Per-lane FIFO is untouched because the skipped frame stays at its lane's head and seeds a later emission. This closes the unbounded starvation the old behavior created for a normal lane holding frames wider than half the ceiling - the live paced-transfer shape, 16384-byte fragments plus header against a 32768 ceiling - with a small bulk or background frame waiting. wide-normal-frames-do-not-end-the-emission-for-waiting-bulk pins it: b0 rides out with the first emission where the old behavior shipped n0 alone and starved b0 until the normal lane ran dry. It is not the whole starvation policy by itself: a head wider than what the lanes above it leave behind is skipped by this rule on every emission rather than once, which is what starvation_guard_is_deleted_but_check_the_hole_first now answers.
reconciled.share_pass_is_inert_in_this_corpus: RATIFIED (Joey, 2026-08-05): fixed. saturated-normal-with-waiting-bulk-and-background and starvation-window-for-a-single-bulk-frame set lane_depth 256, so the normal lane holds 38400 and 46080 queued bytes against the 22937-byte 70 percent ceiling and the share binds. The frozen first emission is 90 normal frames, then b0 (and g0 where present), then the donation pass tops the emission up to 32768 bytes with more normal frames - an order no strict-priority scheduler with full-lane coalescing can produce, which is what makes this corpus discriminate the ratified model from strict priority at all. The swift-ea and kotlin-bt answer files predate the depth change; they are frozen records of deleted code and were not re-run, so their divergence on these two cases in trace-diff is expected.
reconciled.bounded_lanes_backpressure: Ratified. Every lane is bounded and a full lane PARKS the sender; nothing is ever dropped and the link is never torn down. dropped_ids is empty and link_dropped is false in every step of every case here. This deletes two shipping iOS behaviors outright: the 4 MiB high-water shed, where EAAccessoryAdapter discards a queued frame from the lowest occupied lane on each arriving enqueue with no error to the caller (swift-ea drops g0, g1 and g2 in ios-high-water-drops-background; every other arm queues them), and the 8 MiB hard cap, where it tears the session down mid-transfer because it has nothing left to shed (swift-ea sets link_dropped on the 33rd enqueue in ios-hard-cap-drops-the-link). Both become backpressure. This is a user-visible behavior change on a shipping platform, already accepted; recording it here is the record. Its cost is real and belongs with the change: a caller that used to be silently lied to now blocks, so any iOS caller that enqueues from a context that must not block needs a bounded-wait or try-enqueue path.
reconciled.priority_source: Ratified. Priority is the enqueue argument. The platform adapters' peek of frame[5] with a fallback to normal under 16 bytes is deleted, and a-short-frame-loses-its-priority is the evidence of what deleting it changes: swift-ea and kotlin-bt route the 8-byte bulk frame s0 to the NORMAL lane and emit it ahead of n0, while every Rust arm routes it to bulk and emits it behind. The frozen answer is the Rust order (n0 then s0). min_frame_bytes_for_priority disappears from the constant set.
reconciled.configured_ceiling_is_honored: max_emission_bytes is a construction parameter of the shared scheduler and is always honored, so honors_configured_ceiling is true. a-small-emission-ceiling-is-not-honored-everywhere is the injectability probe and swift-ea fails it exactly as designed: it coalesces all six frames into one 384-byte emission against a configured 256, because 32768 is a private Swift constant. Swift's three hardcoded byte thresholds (32768 coalesce cap, 4 MiB high water, 8 MiB hard cap) all die with the adapter. kotlin-bt and rust-driver report null because they have no emission concept at all - one frame per write - which is not a ceiling divergence but the absence of batching, ruled on separately.
reconciled.one_frame_per_write_is_not_a_policy: kotlin-bt and rust-driver emit exactly one frame per drain in every case. That is not a competing emission policy, it is the absence of batching: neither has a max_emission_bytes, so neither can coalesce. Both adopt the shared scheduler's batching wholesale. The visible consequence in this file is that nearly every multi-frame emission diverges from those two arms; treating each of those steps as its own ruling would be noise, so it is one ruling here.
reconciled.lane_depth_is_uniform_and_configured: All three lanes take the same configured depth (64 by default, per-case override). The corpus's capture-phase accommodation - lane_depth applies to bulk and background while the normal lane keeps whatever the arm happens to have - exists because three of the five arms cannot configure the normal lane, and it does not survive into the shared scheduler. Note for the record that this is NOT the shipping daemon value: both OutboundPacker construction sites (rfcomm and network writer tasks) use LANE_CAPACITY = 16, not 64, so the rust-packer arm's constants describe the corpus default rather than what ships. The shared scheduler takes it as configuration; whether the daemon keeps 16 is a separate sizing question, not a conformance one.
reconciled.no_prefetch_stash: A lane is one queue and nothing is held outside it. Two arms prefetch and both report a capacity that is not their configured capacity: OutboundPacker pulls a non-fitting frame out of the channel into `Lane::pending`, freeing an mpsc permit for a parked sender, and the Kotlin writer loop speculatively dequeues as soon as data arrives, which is why bounded-lanes-park-the-sender accepts 5 enqueues at a depth of 4 instead of 4. Ruled: no prefetch, so configured depth is actual depth and the frozen answer accepts exactly 4 and parks exactly 4. This changes no emission anywhere - the prefetched frame seeds the next emission either way - only the accounting.
reconciled.parked_senders_land_between_drains: An emission is built from what is in the lanes at the instant the drain begins; senders unparked by that drain land before the next drain, in enqueue order. This is the rule that makes bounded-lanes-park-the-sender deterministic: the first emission frees exactly four slots and b4 through b7 land, in order, before the second drain composes.
reconciled.fragmentation_is_below_the_scheduler: Asymmetric by design. The scheduler emits whole frames and never splits one across an emission - the network path treats a mid-frame tail as fatal - so fragments_frames is false and an oversize frame ships alone and intact as its own seed (an-oversize-frame-exceeds-the-emission-ceiling: n0 alone at 40960, then n1). EA is the exception and stays one: rust-ea splits n0 into 32768 + 8192 and coalesces n1 onto the tail, because an EA packet has an MTU. Under the restructure that lives in an EA-MTU fragmenter BELOW the scheduler, fed whole frames. The same seam owns stream ids: an EA packet carries one stream-id prefix, so frames from different streams can never share a packet, which is why rust-ea splits same-stream-frames-coalesce-and-streams-never-mix into (n0,n1), (n2), (n3) while this file puts all four in one emission. Both are correct at their own layer; neither is a divergence to reconcile away.
reconciled.starvation_guard_is_deleted_but_check_th: EaChunker's skip-count guard (8 skips, then serve a lower lane once) stays deleted, but the share pass does NOT subsume it and the hole is not confined to the degenerate ceiling this entry originally claimed. A share is a byte ceiling, not a reserved slot: a head wider than floor(max_emission_bytes * share) can never be taken in the share pass, and the donation pass walks the lanes in priority order, so a normal lane that stays fed takes the remainder before the lanes below are reached. Bulk and background then make no progress for as long as normal has frames, at any ceiling, and the emission never ends early because the non-fitting-head rule keeps it going with normal frames. Shipping configurations reach it: the rfcomm writer's 4096-byte ceiling gives bulk 819 bytes and background 409, and the gateway link's 16384-byte ceiling gives bulk 3276 against 8192-byte delivery stream chunks, so an OTA or asset transfer stalls behind ordinary player traffic instead of sharing the link with it. Ratified by Joey 2026-08-11, superseding the acceptance this entry originally recorded: the rule that closes it is byte credit, not a skip count. A lane that an emission passes over entirely banks its share, and once the bank covers its own head that lane takes the next emission's seed, which is the only placement wide enough for a head that exceeds the whole ceiling. A lane that is served banks nothing, so a lane whose frames fit inside its share never triggers it. The starvation window becomes ceil(head_bytes / floor(max_emission_bytes * share)) emissions instead of unbounded. It changes exactly one frozen step: bulk-saturated-background-waits, whose 512-byte ceiling holds one frame, emits g0 on the twelfth drain instead of b11 - the captured rust-ea guard got g0 out at emission 11 for the same reason, which is the closest thing to independent corroboration this corpus has. a-bulk-head-wider-than-its-share-is-not-starved-by-a-fed-normal-lane pins the non-degenerate shape at a ceiling that holds forty frames.
reconciled.cross_lane_queue_cap: Deleted. The Driver's single 16-frame cap across all three lanes is the byte-blind cap the restructure names: it counts frames, so 16 sixteen-kilobyte fragments and 16 sixty-four-byte events cost the same. Per-lane byte-aware bounds replace it, so cross_lane_queue_cap is null.
reconciled.enqueue_couples_to_send: False. rust-driver, rust-ea and swift-ea all couple the caller's enqueue to the write, which is why rust-driver reports every enqueue in this corpus as parked - the shut sink blocks its writer loop, the loop is the only thing draining the command channel, and head-of-line blocking then makes ARRIVAL order beat priority order (strict-priority-baseline emits g0, n0, b0). The shared scheduler is push/pull: enqueue takes a lane slot and returns, and a separate pull builds the emission. Nothing about the emitted order may depend on who is blocked on the link.
reconciled.queued_bytes: Populated everywhere in this file. Only swift-ea accounts bytes today; rust-packer, rust-driver, rust-ea and kotlin-bt all report null, which is the byte-blindness finding the encode-at-enqueue restructure exists to fix. The field stays diagnostic-only - it is state, not behavior - but an arm that still reports null after the cutover has not adopted the restructure.
reconciled.write_complete_is_a_no_op: Every write_complete step is empty, in this file and in all five arms, because a drain in this corpus supplies its own unit of link capacity. Credit-gating (one batch in flight per device, the next send gated on on_write_complete) is real in the restructure but is a property of the transport seam above the scheduler, and this corpus's op vocabulary cannot separate the two. A corpus that wants to pin it needs a drain op that does NOT carry credit.

asymmetries.fragments_frames: EA MTU fragmentation and per-stream packet boundaries sit in a fragmenter below the scheduler, not in it; see reconciled.fragmentation_is_below_the_scheduler.
asymmetries.stream: the corpus stream id is an EA transport concept the scheduler never reads; only rust-ea observes it.
